paragraphs: Seven fostering services list Croydon as an area they cover, all of them independent agencies, and they are shown above. The council also runs its own service, Foster Croydon, which describes itself as one of the highest-paying councils in the south of England after a 30% rise in carer pay. Fostering for the council means looking after Croydon's own children with its social workers behind you; an independent agency assesses, trains and supervises you itself and is asked by councils, Croydon included, to find homes for the children they look after.

The council is clear that it needs more carers. Its market position statement for 2025 to 2027 says that between 525 and 550 Croydon children are in care at any one time, and that in June 2025 227 of the children in foster homes lived with council carers and 189 with carers from independent agencies. In July 2024, 79% of Croydon's children in care lived within 20 miles of the borough, and the council asks for carers who live in Croydon itself.

Its fostering service's annual report for 2025-26 shows interest growing. The service had 152 approved fostering households on 31 March 2026, up from 139 a year earlier, and it received 1,079 requests for information during the year, well above its target of 300. It approved 11 new households and had ten more in assessment at the year end. The report names teenagers, large groups of brothers and sisters, unaccompanied children, children at risk of exploitation and children with disabilities as the children who most need homes, and the service has added specialist and parent and child fostering and is developing emergency care.

Support is local too. Croydon has launched three Horizons Hubs, each led by an experienced foster carer, where carers, their own children and the young people they look after meet, share advice and help one another, with planned sleepovers for a break and support in a crisis. The hubs grew from a pilot with six fostering families.

Foster Croydon pays a weekly allowance for each child, from £208 for children up to 4 to £309 for 16 and 17-year-olds, and a weekly skills fee of £325 at entry level, £450 at the advanced level and £600 for specialist roles, with Council Tax reimbursement and a £1,500 welcome payment for carers who transfer. Our Croydon allowance page sets out the full scale. Talk to the council and two or three of the agencies above before you choose, and see the pages for Bromley, Sutton and Lambeth, or London as a whole, if you live near the borough's edge.
